$4.96/hr and $5.85/hr. Two GPUs, one generation apart, less than a dollar between them per hour. The cheaper option is last year's chip, and it might still be the right call for your workload.

Current Spheron marketplace pricing, subject to availability and may vary by region:

$4.96/hr is on-demand H200, with spot as low as $3.31/hr (33% off).

$5.85/hr is on-demand B300, the lowest bookable on-demand rate on the whole marketplace.

Here's how to choose:

Pick H200 if you run a proven Hopper-class training or inference pipeline and want the lowest cost per token today. The spot rate alone cuts a third off your bill.

Pick B300 instead if you need current-gen Blackwell Ultra silicon for newer model architectures and want the cheapest on-demand entry point on the platform.

Either way, you're not locked in. Switch GPUs or providers from one dashboard without a procurement call.

results.title: Paying full price for every GPU you rent is a rookie mistake. | Spheron Network
results.author: Spheron Network
highlights:
Paying full price for every GPU you rent is a rookie mistake.

Wafer, a YC-backed inference startup, doesn't.

They run Wafer Pass and Wafer Serverless entirely on NVIDIA B300, mixing Spot and dedicated Blackwell Ultra nodes through one API.

Per-minute billing on both means Wafer only pays spot rates when a workload can tolerate interruption, and reserves dedicated B300 capacity for what can't.

Spheron's B300 Spot pricing: $5.81/hr. Nebius runs $7.85/hr for the same tier. AWS's p6-b300 instance is $17.80/hr. CoreWeave won't even post a number, contact sales only.

One dashboard. Spot and dedicated nodes side by side. One bill, billed per minute, no separate contracts to manage, no second invoice to reconcile at the end of the month.

That's the fleet Wafer picked to run two different products off the same B300 capacity.

results.title: H100 Cloud Pricing 2026: Hourly Rates by Provider
results.author: CloudGpu Team
highlights:
## H100 Cloud Pricing 2026: Hourly Rates by Provider

NVIDIA H100 cloud rental costs roughly $1.99/hr on RunPod, $2.49/hr on Lambda Labs, and about $1.87/hr on Vast.ai, dropping to ~$1.03/hr on spot (Spheron). Hyperscalers charge far more — up to ~$12/hr on Azure. The most striking fact about H100 pricing in 2026: the same GPU can cost nearly 14x more on one provider than another.

This guide compares current H100 hourly rates across every major provider, explains why they vary so wildly, and shows how to get the lowest price.

## H100 pricing by provider

Rates below are single-GPU H100 hourly prices as of mid-2026. Note that SXM and PCIe variants differ, and spot prices fluctuate constantly.

| Provider | Type | On-demand ($/hr) | Spot ($/hr) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Spheron | Neo-cloud / marketplace | ~$2.50 | ~$1.03 |
| RunPod | Specialized | $1.99 (Community) / $2.89 (Secure) | ~$1.19 |
| Vast.ai | Marketplace (P2P) | ~$1.49–$1.87 | lower, varies |
| Cudo Compute | Neo-cloud | ~$1.80 | — |
| TensorDock | Marketplace | ~$1.99–$2.25 | — |
| Lambda Labs | Specialized | $2.49–$2.99 (SXM), $3.29 (PCIe) | — |
| CoreWeave | Enterprise neo-cloud | ~$6.16 | + spot |
| AWS (p5) | Hyperscaler | ~$6.88 | ~$2.00–$2.50 |
| GCP (a3) | Hyperscaler | ~$3.00–$11.06 | — |
| Azure | Hyperscaler | ~$12.29 | — |

> ⚠️ H100 spot prices can change multiple times per hour. Every figure here is a snapshot — verify live rates before renting.

The takeaway is clear: neo-clouds and marketplaces cluster around $1.50–$3.00/hr, while hyperscalers run 2–5x higher for the identical GPU. If you don’t need enterprise compliance, paying hyperscaler rates for an H100 is usually overpaying.

## Why do H100 prices vary so much?

A community thread tracking H100 rates across 25 providers found a 13.8x price difference for the same GPU — from $0.80/hr at the cheapest to over $11/hr at the most expensive. That gap comes down to four factors:

Provider tier. Marketplaces pool spare capacity and compete on price; specialized neo-clouds add reliability at a modest premium; hyperscalers charge most for compliance and integration.

Billing model. Spot/interruptible rates undercut on-demand by 50–80%. The Spheron spot floor of ~$1.03/hr versus its $2.50/hr on-demand shows the size of that discount.

GPU variant. The H100 SXM (higher bandwidth, NVLink) and H100 PCIe are priced differently — and how a provider publishes the price matters too. Hyperscalers often quote a full VM (compute, memory, storage bundled), which inflates the headline number versus a “naked GPU” rate.

Region and availability. Capacity-constrained regions cost more, and prices shift as supply changes.

## How H100 prices have fallen

H100 rental has become dramatically cheaper since its 2023 launch. Early adopters paid rates like $7–11/hr on hyperscalers; by 2026 specialist clouds routinely offer the same GPU under $3/hr. The arrival of the B200 (Blackwell) is pushing H100 prices down further as data centers upgrade and demand shifts to newer silicon. If you’re renting H100s, this trend works in your favor — but it also means any quoted price ages quickly.

...

## How to get the cheapest H100

Five tactics get you the lowest H100 rate:

- Use spot pricing. The single biggest lever — spot cuts 50–80% off on-demand. Pair it with frequent checkpointing so interruptions cost minutes.
- Choose a marketplace or neo-cloud. Spheron, Vast.ai, and RunPod consistently undercut hyperscalers. See our cheapest cloud GPU providers breakdown.
- Pick PCIe over SXM if you don’t need the extra bandwidth or multi-GPU NVLink.
- Watch for bundled VM pricing. A hyperscaler’s headline rate may include compute and storage you’re paying for regardless.
- Match the region to availability, and avoid egress fees by keeping data in-region.

...

## The bottom line

H100 cloud pricing in 2026 spans from ~$1.03/hr on spot to over $12/hr on hyperscalers — a nearly 14x spread for the same silicon. The provider tier and billing model, not the GPU itself, decide your bill. Use spot pricing on a neo-cloud or marketplace, watch for bundled VM rates, and verify live prices at deployment, since the H100 market keeps getting cheaper.

...

### What’s the cheapest H100?

 Spot pricing on marketplaces and neo-clouds is cheapest — around $1.03/hr on Spheron spot as of mid-2026, with RunPod spot occasionally near $1.19/hr. The trade-off is interruptibility, so use checkpointing.

results.title: B200 GPU On-Demand Prices Vary 3-4x: From $3.70 to $14.24/Hour, How to Calculate Blackwell's Unit Compute Cost - NexGPU-算力租赁,GPU服务器,GPU云算力,AI服务器租用-新闻博客
results.author: Posts 140
highlights:
The same B200 GPU, why can on-demand unit prices differ by 3-4 times? Third-party cloud price monitoring from June to August 2026 shows a surprisingly wide distribution: Spheron reports $3.70 per hour, Lambda Labs between $4.99 and $5.29, Nebius $5.50, Runpod between $5.89 and $5.98, and AWS's p6-b200 instance converts to as high as $14.24 per hour. The median on-demand price across the web for B200 is around $6.84 per hour. The maximum price difference reaches 3.85 times, which cannot be explained by just "platform premium."

...

## 1. B200 GPU Price Map in August 2026: What's the Difference Between $3.70 and $14.24/Hour

First, look at the facts. According to third-party cloud price monitoring (GetDeploying, CloudZero, etc., data from June-August 2026), B200 GPU on-demand rental prices show significant divergence:

| Platform Type | Platform Example | Hourly Unit Price (USD) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Emerging Compute Cloud | Spheron | $3.70 |
| Emerging Compute Cloud | Lambda Labs | $4.99-$5.29 |
| Emerging Compute Cloud | Nebius | $5.50 |
| Emerging Compute Cloud | Runpod | $5.89-$5.98 |
| Hyperscaler | AWS p6-b200 | $14.24 |
| Web-wide Median | - | $6.84 |

This price gap intuitively reflects differences in platform types. Emerging compute aggregation platforms usually provide compute as "bare metal" or "basic cloud hosts," with more aggressive pricing strategies, making the GPU itself the core selling point. In contrast, hyperscalers like AWS include additional costs in their prices, such as more mature network architecture, persistent storage, SLA guarantees, and technical support—not that emerging platforms lack these, but their positioning and cost structures differ. Therefore, directly comparing "hourly unit prices" horizontally is dangerous; you must clarify which additional services you need.

Key Point: First list your required network, storage, and SLA requirements, then compare unit prices; otherwise, $3.70 and $14.24 are not comparable.

results.title: H100 Rental Prices in 2026: History, Benchmarks, Outlook
results.author: Artem Bukhkalov
highlights:
H100 rental costs $1.40-2.60/hr on neoclouds and $6-12/hr on hyperscalers in 2026. Prices fell from $8/hr in 2023, bottomed in 2025, then rose 40%.

...

Renting an NVIDIA H100 in mid-2026 costs anywhere from $1.38/hr on GPU marketplaces to $12+/hr on hyperscaler on-demand — an 8x spread for identical silicon. The reference benchmark, the Silicon Data H100 Rental Index, sat near $2.53/GPU-hour, while 1-year reserved contracts priced around $2.35/hr in March 2026, up almost 40% from the October 2025 low of $1.70. The H100 has traveled from $8/hr scarcity pricing in 2023 to commodity status — and now back into a tightening cycle.

...

- Current benchmark: ~$2.53/GPU-hour (Silicon Data index, mid-2026); 1-year contracts ~$2.35/hr (March 2026).
- Price history: ~$8/hr peak (2023) → steady decline through 2024 → $1-2/hr trough (2025, low of $1.70 in October) → +40% rebound into 2026.
- The spread is the story: marketplace median $1.70/hr, neocloud median $2.31, hyperscaler median $6.11 — hyperscalers charge ~3.3x the non-hyperscaler median for the same GPU, per Compute Exchange auction data.
- B200 comparison: $3.70-6.00/hr neocloud on-demand, up to $14.24/hr on AWS; full published range $3.75-27/hr.
- Buy vs. rent crossover: used H100s at $6,000-22,000 vs. ~$20,600/year at reserved rental rates puts the ownership breakeven near 18-24 months of high utilization.
- Futures have arrived: CME (Silicon Data index) and ICE (Ornn) GPU compute futures make the forward curve public for the first time.

...

| Period | 1-yr contract / benchmark rate | Market condition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mid-2023 | ~$8.00/hr | Peak scarcity; allocation by relationship |
| 2024 | $3-5/hr, declining | Neocloud capacity wave lands |
| H1 2025 | $2-3/hr | H200/Blackwell arrive; competition compresses margins |
| Oct 2025 | $1.70/hr (low) | Supply overshoot; fears of H100 obsolescence |
| Dec 2025 → Jan 2026 | $2.00 → $2.20 spot (+10% in 4 weeks) | Inference demand inflection |
| Mar 2026 | $2.35/hr 1-yr contracts (+40% off low) | Tightening; Blackwell absorbed upstream |
| Mid-2026 | ~$2.53/hr index | Firm, volatile |

...

The 2025 trough taught the market two things. First, GPU rental is brutally competitive at the commodity end — anyone can rack H100s, and margins collapsed accordingly. Second, demand is not only training: inference growth re-priced “obsolete” hardware. An H100 that lost its training-frontier status remained the workhorse for serving models, and at $1.70/hr it was suddenly the cheapest FLOPS in the market. Buyers noticed; the rebound followed.

## On-demand pricing by provider type, mid-2026

| Provider type | H100 on-demand ($/GPU-hr) | Median (Compute Exchange data) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Marketplaces / boutique clouds | $1.38-1.49 low end | $1.70 |
| Neoclouds (Lambda, Nebius, RunPod, Spheron, etc.) | $1.90-3.50 | $2.31 |
| Hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, GCP) on-demand | $6-12+ (up to $11.68-12.29) | $6.11 |
| Reserved listings, all types | $1.07-10.14 | $5.52 |

Sources: IntuitionLabs GPU pricing index, Compute Exchange, AIMultiple.

Why the hyperscaler premium survives: enterprise procurement inertia, egress and data-gravity lock-in, compliance certifications, and bundled credits. For workloads without those constraints, the same GPU costs 60-75% less one tier down. That arbitrage is the neocloud business model — and its compression is why neocloud margins depend on reserved commitments rather than spot.

...

## B200 comparison

| Metric | H100 (SXM 80GB) | B200 (192GB) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Neocloud on-demand | $1.90-3.50/hr | $3.70-6.00/hr |
| Hyperscaler on-demand | up to $11.68-12.29/hr | up to $14.24/hr (AWS p6); published range to $27 |
| 8-GPU node, neocloud | ~$15-25/hr | ~$29.60/hr (Spheron) |
| 8-GPU node, AWS | — | $113.93/hr ($82,030/month) |
| Training throughput vs H100 | 1x | ~2.5-3x |

Per Spheron’s B200 pricing survey and Silicon Data’s B200 index, which recorded the B200 moving from ~$4.40/hr to spikes above $6.00/hr within a single month in early 2026 — Blackwell remains supply-constrained and correspondingly volatile (spot up 48% between February and April 2026). On per-token economics, a $4.50/hr B200 at ~2.7x throughput beats a $2.35/hr H100; the constraint is getting allocation at all.

...

Four forces, two in each direction:

Upward: (1) inference demand compounding — every deployed model is a permanent load; (2) H100 supply is now fixed — production has shifted to Blackwell/Rubin, so the H100 fleet only shrinks from here.

Downward: (3) Blackwell volume ramps through 2026-27, and each B200 displaces ~2.5-3 H100-equivalents of demand; (4) expiring 2023-24 reservations and fleet upgrades are pushing A100s/H100s onto the secondary market in size in late 2026.

...

Yes. One-year contract rates rose almost 40% from the $1.70/hr October 2025 low to $2.35/hr by March 2026, and the spot index jumped 10% in four weeks over the 2025-26 year-end ($2.00 to $2.20). Drivers: inference workload growth, Blackwell supply absorbed by hyperscalers, and enterprises extending H100 fleet life.

...

How much does a B200 cost to rent compared to an H100?

B200 on-demand spans $3.70-6.00/hr on neoclouds (Spheron from $3.70, Lambda $4.99) and up to $14.24/hr on AWS p6 — published rates span $3.75 to $27 across all providers. That is roughly 2-3x H100 pricing for about 2.5-3x training throughput, so B200 economics per token are competitive when available.
